title: The Virgin asks where the gift comes from

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 11, cols. A-B (PDF p. 35)

source_text: Neque prius sanctissima Virgo donum admisit, quam, quis illud mitteret, et quodnam donum esset, ac quis ferret, addidicisset. Quae, dum secum, velut anceps loqueretur, ait ad Angelum: Unde sic nobis benedictionem apportasti? Ex cuiusmodi thesauris, verbi margarita nobis emissa est? Unde nobis donum materiam paravit? Ex caelo advenisti, at in terra incedis: humanam formam exhibes, et lucis fulgore resplendes.
pass_a_gloss: Nor before (neque prius) did the most holy Virgin admit/accept (admisit) the gift (donum), than she had learned (addidicisset) who was sending it (mitteret), and what gift it was, and who was bearing it (ferret). She, while with herself, as if doubtful (velut anceps), she was speaking (loqueretur), says to the Angel: Whence (unde) thus to us have you brought (apportasti) blessing (benedictio)? From what sort of treasuries (thesauri) has the pearl of the word (verbi margarita) been sent forth (emissa est) to us? Whence for us has the gift prepared (paravit) matter/substance (materia)? From heaven you have come (advenisti), but on earth you walk (incedis): human form (humana forma) you display (exhibes), and with the brightness of light (lucis fulgore) you shine (resplendes).

choices.choice: The Virgin's questions are the author's expansion of the scene, not a Gospel quotation, so nothing is cited.
'Unde nobis donum materiam paravit?' is obscure (literally 'whence has the gift prepared matter for us?'); rendered close to the letter as 'made ready its substance'.
The margin variant 'al. promissum' (perhaps 'promissum' for 'donum', 'the promise') was not adopted.
'et ... resplendes' rendered 'yet you shine' to bring out the contrast set up by the previous clause.

pass_b_english: Nor did the most holy Virgin accept the gift before she had learned who was sending it, what the gift was, and who was bringing it. Speaking with herself as one in two minds, she said to the Angel: From where have you brought us such a blessing? From what treasuries has the pearl of the word been sent out to us? From where has the gift made ready its substance for us? You have come from heaven, yet you walk on earth; you show a human form, yet you shine with the brightness of light.
notes: The Virgin's questions are the author's expansion of the scene, not a Gospel quotation, so nothing is cited. 'Unde nobis donum materiam paravit?' is obscure (literally 'whence has the gift prepared matter for us?'); rendered close to the letter as 'made ready its substance'. The margin variant 'al. promissum' (perhaps 'promissum' for 'donum', 'the promise') was not adopted. 'addidicisset' as printed (from addisco). 'et ... resplendes' rendered 'yet you shine' to bring out the contrast set up by the previous clause.
